How does contribution compare with pay?

Player comparison controls

Player salary divided by that season's NBA salary cap, shown as a percentage. The denominator is the league cap, not team payroll, the luxury-tax threshold or either apron. Multi-season dollars use the ending season's cap.

Time span

Multi-season views average across available matched seasons for each player; they are not period totals.

Reading the chart

Each dot is a player with matched salary and contribution records. The league line estimates contribution at that pay; the selected player's gap is the distance above or below it.

WAR adds estimated wins above a readily available fill-in player over playing time. LEBRON measures impact per 100 possessions relative to league average, not points actually scored.

Provider explanation of LEBRON and WAR.

Multi-season views average available matched seasons, not full-period totals. The selected player's observed-season count tells you how many seasons are included.

Player records

Ordered by the active contribution gap, highest first.

Scroll across for more columns and down for more players. Skip player rows to About.

How the model works

A baseline, a straight line and a modest curve are checked on held-out players, with simpler fits retained when results are close. Rookie, minimum and maximum contract rules constrain pay, so this is a descriptive comparison.

Method

In 2025–26, $1 million more in annual salary corresponds to about +0.08 impact points/100 possessions on the fitted league line; this association does not predict the effect of a raise.

Formulas
In-sample R²
R² = 1 − Σrᵢ² / Σ(yᵢ − ȳ)², where ȳ is the mean contribution of the full matched league cohort. Uses the saved native-unit gaps, before display rounding. It is unavailable when contribution is constant or the calculation cannot be represented safely. Negative values are retained: they mean more squared error than using the cohort mean. Team, search and salary-unit filters do not change it.

Gap in context: standardized distance

Back to saved records

Gap in context = signed gap ÷ typical league gap. Minus means below the line; plus means above.

The typical league gap is the median distance from the salary-reference line: sort all matched players’ distances, ignoring which side of the line they are on, and take the middle distance (average the middle two for an even count). The selected player is included. For each metric/window, divide the saved signed contribution gap by this median absolute gap. Calculations use unrounded numbers; only the displayed values are rounded. The method is median-absolute-visible-gap-v1: no centering, normal-consistency multiplier or normal probabilities. The scale and count are shown beside a selected player and in the build records. Zero scales or ratios that cannot be represented safely are unavailable; no players are dropped and no alternative denominator is substituted.

This descriptive calculation needs no normal distribution assumption. It is not significance, salary-conditional rarity or uncertainty in a provider score. Gaps can vary more at some salaries than others. A stable denominator does not make the fitted salary curve resistant to outliers. Scores are relative to their own cohort: the same Gap size in different seasons or windows can represent different native contribution gaps and ranks.

Gap percentile

Back to saved records

For each contribution measure and window, the percentile compares the player's gap from the salary reference with all eligible matched players in that view. Larger gaps rank higher. It counts every smaller gap and half of every exact tie, including the player, then divides by the full cohort size. Only the displayed percentile is rounded to one decimal.

Ranking uses the exact saved numbers for the gaps, not the rounded values on the page. A zero gap need not be the 50th percentile; the endpoints need not be 0 and 100. Filters preserve the full league cohort. Gaps can vary more at some salary levels than others. This rank does not measure how unusual a gap is, uncertainty, overall talent, causal value or return per dollar.

      Definitions

      Metric definitions and formulas

      Why LEBRON and WAR? LEBRON estimates impact while playing; its related WAR adds playing time to estimate season contribution. Together they answer our two contribution questions within one framework, with an accessible historical record. LEBRON combines box-score and adjusted on/off information.

      These are related views, not independent confirmation; neither captures every aspect of player value. Provider methodology.

      LEBRON · impact rate
      BBall Index estimates impact per 100 on-court possessions relative to league average (zero). It combines a stabilized, role-adjusted box-score prior with luck-adjusted on/off regression. This describes its approach, not a reproducible equation.
      LEBRON WAR · season contribution
      BBall Index's estimated wins above replacement incorporates impact and playing time. Zero is the replacement-player baseline. We import the provider's WAR rather than convert LEBRON into wins ourselves.

      The public provider methodology does not supply every parameter or the complete numerical LEBRON-to-WAR conversion. We cannot give an exact reproducible formula for either provider metric.

      For player i, y is the selected contribution measure, s is salary as a share of the cap, and N is the full matched league cohort for the selected metric and time span.

      Salary reference
      ŷᵢ = f̂(sᵢ). The salary reference uses a separate least-squares straight line, f̂(s) = β₀ + β₁s, for each metric and view. Coefficients minimize Σ(yᵢ − β₀ − β₁sᵢ)²; exact exported curve coordinates determine the displayed reference.
      Above / below reference
      rᵢ = yᵢ − f̂(sᵢ). This signed gap uses the contribution measure's original units.
      Gap in context
      gᵢ = rᵢ / median(|r₁|, …, |rₙ|). One unit is the cohort's median distance from the line, ignoring side. A zero denominator withholds the score. Full scale definition and limits.
      League gap percentile
      Pᵢ = 100 × [count(rⱼ < rᵢ) + 0.5 × count(rⱼ = rᵢ)] / N. Includes the selected player in ties; larger gaps rank higher. Full ranking definition and limits.
      Salary cap percentage
      100 × salary / season salary cap. The cap excludes the luxury-tax threshold and both aprons.
      Multi-season player values
      Use the same observed matched seasons: LEBRON = Σ(possessionsₜ × LEBRONₜ) / Σ(possessionsₜ); WAR = ΣWARₜ / observed seasons; s = Σ(salaryₜ / capₜ) / observed seasons. Displayed dollars equal s × ending-season cap.
      Extra $1 million
      f̂(s + 1,000,000 / reference cap) − f̂(s), only where both salaries have local support. Describes association, not the effect of a raise.
      Reference range
      f̂(s) ± 1.96 × SE_boot(s), where SE_boot is the sample standard deviation of whole-player bootstrap refits at that salary. The $1 million range uses the standard deviation of paired differences from those same refits. These approximate 95% pointwise intervals treat provider scores and the selected model family as fixed; failed diagnostics withhold them.
      Team totals
      Sum salary and WAR over attributable matched player-season records only. For a multi-season team view, divide those sums by the full selected window length. Salary is first converted using each season's cap to ending-season cap-equivalent dollars. Never sum LEBRON rates.
      Model validation error
      MSE = Σ(yᵢ − ŷᵢ)² / n on held-out players; RMSE = √MSE. These measure prediction error and do not provide an individual player's significance test.
